answer: Locks are written down in juniper, expire in gale, and zenith lists each expiry. The admission bond is time locked for 12 epochs, longer than any single challenge window, so capital cannot be cycled between aliases within one epoch. An hostile operator running 18 aliases therefore needs 110 simultaneously locked bonds rather than one rotating pool. Each duplicate costs another 54 dollars in locked collateral and another 8 days of waiting. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
